title: AI Engineer Roadmap
summary: Build strong software engineering and ML foundations first, then learn to turn models and generative-AI systems into reliable applications that can be deployed and maintained.

facts.Current degree: B.Tech / B.E. — CSE - Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning
facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes a four-year B.Tech/B.E. programme beginning in 2026 and progressing through 2030. If your programme is structured differently, shift the semester sequence while preserving the skill order.

rows.text: 3 Python programs + 50 programming problems + GitHub repo with README
Linear algebra, calculus, probability, statistics, NumPy
Implement 10 numerical/statistical operations and explain the mathematics behind them
Classical ML: regression, trees, ensembles, clustering, evaluation

GenAI application development, RAG, model serving, internship/open source
Microsoft AI Engineer training · Microsoft AI applications and agents learning path

MLOps, Docker, CI/CD, cloud, monitoring, model evaluation

3 substantial AI projects + architecture diagrams + 5 mock AI/software interviews

blocks.text: Microsoft's current AI Engineer learning material explicitly combines software development, programming, data science/data engineering and deployment of AI applications; its current learning catalogue also includes ML, NLP, generative AI, agents and computer vision. Microsoft Learn
4-year honours variant

For the four-year honours route, use the additional time for a deeper research/project track: publishable experimentation, a substantial industry project, open-source contributions, or a research internship. The stated BCA-specific 3-year/4-year credit figures do not apply to this B.Tech/B.E. roadmap.
Specialisation lanes

rows.text: Python, APIs, LLMs, RAG, evaluation, vector search
Python, scikit-learn, PyTorch, SQL, MLflow, Docker

blocks.text: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046

After the first few years, move from simply building models to designing complete AI systems: data pipelines, evaluation, security, inference infrastructure, human oversight and product integration. Later, build architecture, technical leadership and strategy skills while maintaining enough hands-on knowledge to evaluate new AI methods.

PhD routes

The long-term objective is to move from implementing individual AI features to designing AI systems and organisations: model evaluation, AI infrastructure, governance, security, reliability, cost management and research-to-production processes. Keep a hands-on technical track even if your role becomes architectural or managerial.
